why: P2a shipped 2.0.0 without an absolute acquire/release ns/op baseline, so its assertOps assertion has no recorded referent. This records a differential A-vs-B baseline instead: the shipped ObjectPool.js against the frozen byte-identical 2.0.0 copy (test/baseline/ObjectPool-2.0.0.js), measured with compareOps. Because the four hot bodies are hash-identical across A and B, the true ns/op ratio is 1.0 and any deviation is pure timing noise; this file records the measured noise floor and the threshold chosen above it.
lane: 1:1 acquire+release churn at capacity on a preallocated size=4096 pool (exercises both hot bodies per op)
statistic: min over N=9 runs of max(A/B, B/A) of opsPerSec (symmetric ns/op ratio); min-over-N floors one-sided scheduling/GC jitter the same way T6 floors allocation noise

sweep.note: 1.15 sits ~10x above the clean min-over-9 deviation (<=1.014) and ~3.4x below the positive control (>=3.89): it rejects a real regression yet never trips on noise. A bare single-run 1.05 was inside the noise floor (single-run max reached 1.11) and would have been flaky; min-over-9 plus 1.15 is the honest gate.
